title: A signed finite sum of coerced naturals is the coerced natural sum
statement: `Int.sumRange (fun k => Int.ofNat (f k)) n = Int.ofNat (Nat.sumRange f n)`. The bridge that lets a lattice-point COUNT -- which lives in the naturals, and which `Nat.countRectangle_partition` produces -- enter a signed identity. Both steps are free: `Int.add (ofNat a) (ofNat b)` is definitionally `ofNat (Nat.add a b)` at SYMBOLIC arguments, because `Int.add`'s `ofNat`/`ofNat` minor premise is literally `ofNat (Nat.add m n)`, and `Int.zero` is definitionally `ofNat 0`. So the induction is `Eq.refl` at the base and one congruence at the step. `Kernel::axiom_footprint` is EMPTY. Admitted by the trusted gate on the first attempt.

formal.statement: theorem Int.sumRange_ofNat : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> AxNat)) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} Int (Int.sumRange (fun (x2 : AxNat) => Int.ofNat (x0 x2)) x1) (Int.ofNat (AxNat.sumRange x0 x1))))
